mainTopic: Why one who is liable to death is exempt from paying (the rule of רבי נחוניא בן הקנה), and the difference between the reasons of אביי and רבא
overview: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא which shows that after the courts stopped judging capital cases, Heaven still brings each sinner a death that matches his court penalty. From this it learns that a lion and bandits count as בידי שמים, while cold and heat count as בידי אדם, so it reverses an earlier statement. רבא then gives his own source for רבי נחוניא בן הקנה's rule: a פסוק about מולך compares כרת to court death, so כרת also exempts from payment. The difference between אביי and רבא is a זר who ate תרומה: אביי exempts him from paying, and רבא makes him pay. The גמרא challenges אביי using רב חסדא's case of stolen חלב, where the theft comes before the sin. It defends אביי by narrowing the case step by step: someone else put the food into the זר's mouth, then straight into his throat, where he could bring it back up only with great effort. רב פפא instead says it was liquid תרומה, and רב אשי begins a third answer, a זר eating his own תרומה, which continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Heaven still carries out the four court death penalties
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא continues quoting a ברייתא. After the courts stopped judging capital cases, each guilty person still dies in a way that matches his court penalty, and lions and bandits are among the ways Heaven does this.
steps.simpleTranslation: The judgment of the four death penalties did not stop. Someone liable for stoning either falls from a roof or is mauled by a wild animal. Someone liable for burning either falls into a fire or is bitten by a snake. Someone liable for beheading is either handed over to the government or attacked by bandits. Someone liable for strangling either drowns in a river or dies of a throat disease. So how can lions and thieves be counted as harm from people?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is in the middle of quoting a ברייתא as a challenge. The ברייתא shows that a wild animal and bandits are tools Heaven uses to carry out death sentences.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, lions and thieves were treated as harm 'by man' and cold and heat as harm 'from Heaven.' But this ברייתא says a beast mauling someone and bandits attacking him are Heaven's way of punishing a sinner. So these must be בידי שמים, which goes against the earlier statement.

keyTerms.meaning: The four death penalties of בית דין: stoning, burning, beheading, strangling

steps.confusionAlert: This list is not a new law about court cases. It is quoted only to show that a lion and bandits are ways Heaven acts, which sets up the reversal in the next step.

phrases.english: the judgment of the four death penalties was not abolished.
One who was liable to stoning
either falls from the roof
or a wild animal mauls him.
And one who was liable to burning
either falls into a fire
or a snake bites him.
And one who was liable to beheading
either is handed over to the government
or bandits attack him.
And one who was liable to strangling
either drowns in a river
or dies of a choking disease?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא quoted at the end of the previous עמוד as a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier statement that lions and thieves are harm בידי אדם and cold and heat are בידי שמים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists a beast mauling and bandits attacking as Heaven's way of carrying out death sentences, so they must be בידי שמים.

steps.title: Reverse the earlier statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the challenge and flips the earlier statement: lions and thieves are from Heaven, and cold and heat are from people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, reverse it: a lion and thieves are from Heaven, and cold and heat are from people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by swapping the two categories it had stated before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lion or bandit attack is something a person cannot control, so it is בידי שמים, just as the ברייתא shows. Cold and heat can be avoided if a person is careful, so harm from them counts as בידי אדם, meaning his own carelessness.

keyTerms.meaning: Reverse it, swap the two sides
By human hands (here, through a person's own carelessness)
Cold and heat (from the פסוק in משלי)

phrases.english: Rather, reverse it:
a lion and thieves are by the hand of Heaven,
cold and heat are by the hands of man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge from the ברייתא by reversing the earlier statement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Lions and thieves were thought to be harm בידי אדם, and cold and heat בידי שמים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Lions and thieves are בידי שמים; cold and heat are בידי אדם.
steps.whatToRemember: A lion and bandits count as בידי שמים, since Heaven sends them. Cold and heat count as בידי אדם, since a person can protect himself from them.

steps.title: רבא's source: כרת is like court death
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different source for רבי נחוניא בן הקנה: the פסוק about מולך places כרת right after court death, which teaches that כרת exempts from payment just as court death does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The reason of רבי נחוניא בן הקנה comes from here: 'And if the people of the land hide their eyes from that man when he gives his children to מולך... then I will set My face against that man and his family and cut him off.' The Torah is saying: My כרת is like your death penalty. Just as your death penalty exempts from payments, so too My כרת exempts from payments.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings his own source for the rule that one liable to כרת is exempt from paying. It differs from אביי's source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says that if the court fails to execute the מולך worshipper, ה׳ will punish him with כרת, so it puts כרת in place of court death. רבא learns from this that כרת works like court death: just as court death exempts from payment, so does כרת. רבא's source is only about כרת, not every kind of death בידי שמים.

keyTerms.meaning: An idol to which children were passed through fire
Being 'cut off,' a punishment from Heaven

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a real difference between אביי and רבא, which the גמרא is about to spell out.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא בֶּן הַקָּנָה מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: the reason of Rabbi Neḥunya ben HaKana is from here:
"And if the people of the land do at all hide
their eyes from that man
when he gives of his children to Molech,

phrases.aramaic: וְשַׂמְתִּי אֲנִי אֶת פָּנַי בָּאִישׁ הַהוּא
phrases.english: then I will set My face against that man
and against his family, and I will cut him off."
The Torah said:
My karet is like your death penalty.
Just as with your death penalty
he is exempt from payments,
so too with My karet
he is exempt from payments.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר, טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא בֶּן הַקָּנָה מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about בידי שמים and gives an alternative source to אביי's for רבי נחוניא בן הקנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כרת is compared to court death, so one liable to כרת is exempt from payment.

steps.title: What is the difference between אביי and רבא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the two sources lead to any practical difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between רבא and אביי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a practical case where אביי's source and רבא's source would give different rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree with רבי נחוניא בן הקנה that כרת exempts from payment. The question is whether their different sources ever change the law.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference is there between them?

phrases.english: What difference is there between Rava and Abaye?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares רבא's new source with אביי's earlier one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical case where אביי and רבא would rule differently.

steps.title: A זר who ate תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The difference is a זר who ate תרומה: אביי exempts him from payment and רבא makes him pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them: a non-כהן who ate תרומה. According to אביי he is exempt; according to רבא he must pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that they argue about a זר who ate תרומה on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זר who eats תרומה is liable to death בידי שמים, not כרת. אביי learns that any death בידי שמים exempts from payment, so he is exempt. רבא's source covers only כרת, so this זר must pay.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion given to a כהן, forbidden to a זר

steps.whatToRemember: אביי: any death בידי שמים exempts from payment. רבא: only כרת exempts. Their difference is a זר who ate תרומה.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them:
a non-priest who ate teruma.
phrases.notes: He is liable to death בידי שמים, but not to כרת. That is the whole point of the difference.

phrases.english: According to Abaye he is exempt;
and according to Rava he is liable.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A זר who ate תרומה is exempt according to אביי and must pay according to רבא.

steps.title: רב חסדא's stolen חלב case challenges אביי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how אביי can exempt the זר. רב חסדא taught that a thief who eats stolen חלב must pay, because the theft happened when he lifted it, before the sin of eating. The same should be true of the תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is he really exempt according to אביי?! Didn't רב חסדא say that רבי נחוניא בן הקנה agrees that if someone steals his friend's חלב and eats it, he must pay, because he was already liable for theft before he came to the sin of eating חלב? We see that from the moment he lifted it, he acquired it, and he only became liable to death once he ate it. Here too, from the moment he lifted the תרומה he acquired it, and he only became liable to death once he ate it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's ruling that a זר who ate תרומה is exempt, using a teaching of רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exemption only applies when the obligation to pay and the death penalty start at the same moment. With stolen חלב, the payment obligation started when he lifted it, and the death penalty only when he ate it, so he pays. The זר also lifts the תרומה before eating it, so he should pay even according to אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden fat, whose eating carries כרת
He lifted it (an act that acquires the object)

steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא does not disagree with רבי נחוניא בן הקנה. The thief pays only because the theft came first, at a separate earlier moment, before the death penalty began.

phrases.english: And according to Abaye he is exempt?!
But didn't Rav Ḥisda say:
Rabbi Neḥunya ben HaKana concedes
regarding one who steals his friend's forbidden fat and eats it
that he is liable to pay,
since he was already liable for theft
before he came to the prohibition of forbidden fat.
Apparently, from the moment he lifted it, he acquired it,
but he was not liable with his life
until he ate it.
Here too,
phrases.notes: "Here" means the זר who ate תרומה.

phrases.english: at the moment he lifted it, he acquired it,
and he is not liable with his life
until he eats it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's side of the difference given in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's ruling that a זר who ate תרומה is exempt from payment.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Lifting acquires the item and creates the duty to pay before the eating that brings the death penalty. Since the two do not happen at the same moment, the exemption should not apply.

steps.title: Someone else pushed it into his mouth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that אביי is speaking of a case where someone else stuffed the תרומה into the זר's mouth, so there was no earlier lifting.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Where his friend stuffed the תרומה into his mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends אביי by limiting his ruling to a case with no earlier lifting by the זר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If someone else pushed the תרומה into his mouth, the זר never lifted it himself. So there is no earlier act of taking it, and the duty to pay and the death penalty both come from the eating itself. Since both happen together, אביי's exemption works.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (limits the case)

steps.whatToRemember: Payment is exempt only when the duty to pay and the death penalty begin at the same moment.

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
Where his friend stuffed it
into his mouth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The זר lifted the תרומה himself, so he became obligated to pay before he became liable to death.
steps.terutzMaskana: Someone else put it in his mouth, so ownership and the death penalty come at the same moment, and אביי exempts him.

steps.title: Chewing comes before swallowing
steps.stepSummary: Even if the תרומה was stuffed into his mouth, he acquires it when he chews and is liable to death only when he swallows, so the payment still comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, once he chewed it he acquired it, but he is not liable with his life until he swallows it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from Step 7. Even with stuffed food, the two liabilities do not happen at the same moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that a death liability cancels payment only works when both happen at the same moment. Chewing already makes the תרומה his, because it is ruined for the כהן. The sin of eating is only complete when he swallows. So the payment comes first and should not be cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: He acquired it, and so must pay for it
Liable with his life (a death liability)

phrases.english: In the end, once he chewed it, he acquired it,

phrases.aramaic: מִתְחַיֵּיב בְּנַפְשׁוֹ לָא הָוֵי עַד דְּבַלְעַהּ!
phrases.english: but he is not liable with his life until he swallows it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the case offered in Step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the תרומה was stuffed into the זר's mouth
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Chewing makes it his before swallowing completes the sin, so the payment still comes earlier than the death liability.

steps.title: Pushed straight into the throat
steps.stepSummary: The case is one where the food was pushed directly into his throat, so there was no chewing at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where someone pushed it into his throat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by narrowing the case even more. The food went straight into his throat, so there is no chewing step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With no chewing, the only act is the swallow. The acquiring and the sin now happen together at the same moment, so אביי's exemption works again.

keyTerms.meaning: The throat, the place of swallowing

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן שֶׁתָּחַב לוֹ לְתוֹךְ בֵּית הַבְּלִיעָה.
phrases.english: It is a case where someone pushed it into his throat.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּגוֹן שֶׁתָּחַב לוֹ לְתוֹךְ בֵּית הַבְּלִיעָה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The זר chewed the stuffed food and acquired it before swallowing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The food went straight into his throat, so acquiring and sinning happen together.

steps.title: Could he bring it back up or not?
steps.stepSummary: If he can bring the food back up, he should do so. If he cannot, why is he liable at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If he can bring it back up, let him bring it back. If he cannot bring it back, why is he liable?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new case with two options, and both seem to fail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he could easily bring it back up, he should, and then he would not pay. If he chose not to, he has made it his before the sin. If he truly cannot bring it up, it was forced on him completely, so why should he be liable for anything?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the details?
To bring it back, to return it

phrases.english: What is the case?
If he can bring it back up, let him bring it back.

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָא מָצֵי לְאַהְדּוֹרַהּ — אַמַּאי חַיָּיב?
phrases.english: If he cannot bring it back up, why is he liable?
phrases.notes: Someone else did it to him, and he had no way to stop it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the narrowed case of Step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: The case of food pushed into the throat
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two options: if he can bring it back, the acquiring still comes first. If he cannot, he is fully forced and should not be liable.

steps.title: He could bring it back only with great effort
steps.stepSummary: The case is a middle one: he could bring it back up, but only with great difficulty.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only where he can bring it back up with great effort.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a middle case that sits between the two options of Step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because bringing it up was possible, swallowing is not completely forced on him, so he can be liable. Because it was very hard, he did not acquire it by failing to bring it up beforehand. So the acquiring and the sin still meet at the swallow.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for (a specific case)

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's exemption needs the acquiring and the death liability to happen at the exact same moment. That is why the גמרא keeps narrowing the case.

phrases.english: It is needed only
where he can bring it back up with great effort.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּמָצֵי לְאַהְדּוֹרַהּ עַל יְדֵי הַדְּחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two-sided קשיא of Step 10
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He either can easily bring it back or cannot at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: He can, but only with great effort, so he is liable, and the acquiring and the sin meet at the swallow.

steps.title: רב פפא: liquids of תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains אביי's case differently: someone poured liquids of תרומה into the זר's mouth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is a case where his friend poured liquids of תרומה into his mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a different way to set up אביי's case, without the throat details.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no chewing with liquid. Once it is in his mouth it is ruined and goes down, so the acquiring and the sin come together. This avoids the problems raised in Steps 8 and 10.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
It is a case where his friend poured
liquids of teruma into his mouth.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: כְּגוֹן שֶׁתָּחַב לוֹ חֲבֵירוֹ מַשְׁקִין שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the chewing problem of Step 8, instead of the throat case in Steps 9–11
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Solid food stuffed into the mouth leads to the chewing problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: Liquid has no chewing step, so acquiring and sinning happen together.

steps.title: רב אשי: a זר who ate his own תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי starts another answer: the case is a זר who ate תרומה that belonged to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: It is about a זר who ate his own תרומה,
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי opens a third way to explain אביי's case. His sentence continues past this point, so the גמרא is setting up the rest of his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תרומה was his own, he did not steal it when he picked it up. So רב חסדא's problem about lifting the food first does not apply here. The full payment question is explained in the words that follow.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
It is about a non-priest who ate his own teruma,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: בְּזָר שֶׁאָכַל תְּרוּמָה מִשֶּׁלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third alternative answer after רב פפא's
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative case setup (continues past this point)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The זר stole the תרומה, so lifting it made him owe payment before the sin.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תרומה was his own, so there was no theft when he lifted it.
